name: showreel-c3-blue-sky

voice.text: Why is the sky blue, but sunsets red? Sunlight carries every colour of the rainbow. Our air is full of tiny molecules, mostly nitrogen and oxygen. Blue light hits them and scatters everywhere. Red light mostly passes straight through. So blue reaches your eyes from all over the sky. At sunset, the light crosses far more air. The blue is scattered away on the journey. Only reds and oranges make it through.

caption:
Same sunlight, two colours: why the sky is blue at noon and red at sunset, in one zoom. 🌅
